intended_object: An auxiliary indexing of the generators of the defining ideal of the upper-unitriangular group U_n inside GL_n: x_ij for i > j, x_ii − 1, and 0 (a padding value) for i < j. Inferred from the docstring, the module documentation, and its only use as the generating family in `UnitriangularCoordinateRing.ideal`.
explanation: `relation` exists only so that `ideal` can be written as `Ideal.span (Set.range fun p => relation K ι p.1 p.2)`. Every other use of it (`relation_mem`, `quotient_lower`, `quotient_diag`, the generator checks in the Hopf-ideal proof) only serves to work with that ideal. The function is defined on all pairs (i, j) and returns 0 on strictly upper pairs. That makes the generating family easy to write as a `Set.range`, but it has no counterpart in the literature, where the object is the set of defining equations or the ideal they generate, not a function on ι × ι padded with zeros. The real mathematical objects are `ideal` and `CoordinateRing`. The definition is correct: for j < i it gives the lower entry x_ij, for i = j it gives x_ii − 1, and otherwise 0, which adds nothing to the span. So the ideal is exactly (x_ij for i > j, x_ii − 1), the standard defining ideal of U_n as in Milne 2.9. The orientation matches `universal_upper`, which shows the universal matrix becomes upper triangular in the quotient, and `quotient_diag`, which shows its diagonal becomes 1. The base is any commutative ring K with any finite linearly ordered index type, which is the natural generality. Mathlib has no unitriangular group scheme.
